subject.title: [Bug]: Install bug:No matching version found for node-domexception@1.0.28

question: Which dependency-resolution strategy should own the `node-domexception` source-install fix, and may an external PR carry the final root dependency graph change?
rationale: The issue is valid, but the obvious `2.0.2` override has a documented build-compatibility blocker and root dependency graph changes require maintainer/security authorization.

options.title: Maintainer-owned dependency fix
options.body: A maintainer applies the selected resolver target, regenerates dependency artifacts, updates guard tests, and authorizes the final dependency graph.

options.title: Rework the linked contributor PR
options.body: The existing open PR can remain the candidate if it changes to a compatible target and receives dependency/security approval for its exact head.

options.title: Keep collecting install evidence
options.body: Maintainers can defer implementation until a live reproduction narrows the registry-mirror failure mode further, leaving source installs at risk in the meantime.

recommendation.title: Maintainer-owned dependency fix
recommendation.body: A maintainer applies the selected resolver target, regenerates dependency artifacts, updates guard tests, and authorizes the final dependency graph.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the exact alias guard and later maintained the workspace override metadata, making them the best history-backed owner for the dependency strategy choice.
